title: Jensen Huang is out of Nvidia, but his family is still inside. What roles do his kids Madison and Spencer hold?

 world Jensen Huang is out of Nvidia, but his family is still inside. What roles do his kids Madison and Spencer hold?
 The former CEO's daughter, son and son-in-law Nico Caprez all hold key roles at Nvidia Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his family face mounting scrutiny over their roles at the company following his admission of infidelity and sudden resignation. PHOTO: Reuters file PUBLISHED ON November 14, 2026 8:00 AM BY Helmy Sa'at A tidal wave has swept through the tech world following the shock resignation of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang as president, chief executive officer and board member on Thursday (Nov 12), ending his 33-year tenure at the company.
 In its official announcement, Nvidia said its board had appointed chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim chief CEO while it searches for a permanent successor, with Harvey C. Jones named the company's first-ever chairman of the board. 
 While Wall Street digests what comes next for the chipmaker, the leadership shake-up has intensified scrutiny of Huang's family, with his daughter Madison, son Spencer and son-in-law Nico Caprez all holding influential positions within the technology giant.
 Recent reports, including one by The Wall Street Journal on Sunday, have examined the responsibilities entrusted to the three family members and raised questions about their influence within Nvidia. 
 In a Forbes commentary on Tuesday, contributor Dr Shaheena Janjuha-Jivraj argued that the situation highlighted the challenges of overlapping family and business interests, describing it as "a family business crisis, unfolding inside a company most people would never call a family business".
 Who are the three Huang family members still inside Nvidia, and what do they do? 
 The Huang family trio making their mark at Nvidia
 1. Madison Huang: Physical AI marketing lead 
 Madison, who is Nvidia's senior director of product and technical marketing for physical AI platforms, oversees initiatives involving Omniverse, Cosmos and Isaac, which support industrial simulation and robotics development. 
 Before joining Nvidia in 2020, she studied culinary arts at the Culinary Institute of America and Le Cordon Bleu, worked in marketing for luxury goods group LVMH and obtained an MBA from London Business School.
 2. Spencer Huang: From cocktail bar founder to robotics 
 Her brother Spencer works in product management for Nvidia's robotics division. 
 Like his sister, he took an unconventional route into the technology industry. He co-founded R&D Cocktail Lab, a cocktail bar in Taipei, before pursuing an MBA at New York University and joining the company in 2022.
 3. Nico Caprez: The ‘consigliere’ 
 Madison's husband, Nico Caprez, is Nvidia's vice-president of global AI infrastructure growth, and Fortune reported on Monday that a cloud executive had described him as Jensen's "consigliere" (or trusted adviser), suggesting he could play a significant role in the company's succession planning. 
 'Just as I can be fired, the next CEO has to be hired'
 The prominent roles held by Madison, Spencer and Caprez have fuelled speculation over whether the Huang family could tighten its grip on Nvidia's future as the board searches for a permanent chief . 
 Prior to Huang's resignation, Fortune reported on Monday that Caprez could emerge as a potential successor, while Madison has also been floated in industry circles as a possible candidate for the top job. 
 However, Huang himself recently pushed back against the idea of automatic family succession. In a Bloomberg interview for The Circuit, recorded on Oct 14 and released on Thursday, he said: "Just as I can be fired, the next CEO has to be hired," according to Business Insider. 
 What triggered the crisis? 
 Huang’s exit caps a turbulent week sparked by revelations about his personal life. 
 In a message to Nvidia employees published on the company's newsroom on Sunday, Huang admitted that he had been unfaithful to his wife, Lori, saying his actions had hurt her and their children and that there was no excuse for what he had done. 
 He took responsibility for his actions, saying: "My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do," before asking the public to respect his family's privacy. 
 His wife, Lori Huang, has not publicly commented on her husband's admission as at Friday.
